scope: Three acceptance gates only: R2-1 result contract, R2-2 real business probe, R2-3 terminal state and real exit codes. No M4 rework, no H1-H4 changes, no crypto rewrite, no formal 1000-trial run.

R2_1_result_contract.problem: the validator mixed run success with evidence validity and only checked a handful of fields; it accepted failures declared PASS, duplicate trial ids, an empty PASS run, unknown statuses, wrong authenticated identity, skipped garbled event lines, negative resource values and wrong success_pct/probe statistics; it panicked on empty suites and short SIDs; it never read the real process exit code
R2_1_result_contract.fix: internal/bench/schema.go defines the contract once as tables (required keys, allowed types including null-or-int and float, minimum ranges, empty-string whitelist, enumerations for run_kind/mode/status/denominator). JudgeResults consumes them and returns ResultJudgement with SEPARATE run_status and evidence_status plus acceptance_passed and expected_exit_code. Duplicate JSON keys are rejected; index access is guarded so malformed input yields structured problems instead of a panic; garbled event lines are diagnosed; confirmations must match run/device/SID/operation and must not match twice; every published summary field is recomputed from the raw rows and compared (floats with an explicit tolerance).
invariants: PASS requires requested>0, requested/started/completed consistent, failures=0, not_started=0 and every trial backed by phase facts and a gateway confirmation
FAIL and INCOMPLETE each have their own consistency requirement, not just an exit-code check
a fully recorded real failure is VALID evidence and a FAIL run, never rewritten into a success
R2_1_result_contract.tests: positive control plus failed-but-PASS, duplicate trial ids, empty run, unknown status, empty suites / short SID (panic guard), 8 systematic missing-key cases, duplicate JSON key, wrong authenticated identity, garbled event line, and 9 wrong-summary-field cases

R2_2_real_probe.problem: bench hand-wrote applied:true/duplicate:false and did not share the production device's range check, idempotency or state update
R2_2_real_probe.fix: app.HandleControl is now the one control handler, used by BOTH the production Device loop and the harness: parse -> operation validation -> production range 100..60000 ms -> per-session operation idempotency -> real interval update -> ACK built from the real state. app.ControlSession holds the state actually in effect. Trials record control_applied / control_duplicate / applied_interval_ms. EventSink is notification-driven (bounded signal) instead of a 10 ms poll, with no loss of events that arrived first.
R2_2_real_probe.tests: 1 ms and 60001 ms rejected; 5000 ms actually applied; a repeated operation does not repeat the side effect; handshake_success stays true while probe_success is false when the confirmation never arrives

R2_3_exit_and_evidence.problem: handled failures after RUNNING was written returned directly (leaving RUNNING); write/sync/close errors were ignored; the events file was closed before the producers were stopped; the CLI used a code guessed from the summary; no signal handling; no real Run-level tests; cmd/bench had no tests
R2_3_exit_and_evidence.fix: a single finalize() writes the terminal state for every handled failure and, when even that cannot be written, reports the root cause on stderr and returns a real non-zero code instead of faking a file. Write/Sync/Close errors are checked; producers are stopped and awaited before the events file is closed; the CLI uses the code Run actually returned (the guessing helper was deleted) and separates internal, validator and process exit codes; signals become context cancellation; uncatchable termination is documented as observable only by the parent (ABORTED).
R2_3_exit_and_evidence.tests: real Run integration: setup failure via temp-directory fault injection with an injection-effectiveness guard; cancellation producing INCOMPLETE with the requested count preserved; cmd/bench tests for formal refusal, missing arguments, unknown mode and defective-result verification

cancellation_callback_interleave.finding: the risk the review raised against the old M5A-R1 baseline was REAL in the current code: context.AfterFunc's Stop does not wait for a running callback, so a callback that had passed its generation check and was then descheduled applied deadline=now over the next operation's freshly installed deadline
cancellation_callback_interleave.reproduction: deterministic regression TestCancelCallbackDoesNotClobberNextOperationDeadline parked the old callback at exactly that point with a barrier setter; before the fix it failed with the stale deadline (m=+30.003s) overwriting m=+600s
cancellation_callback_interleave.fix: ioGuard (mutex + sequence) serialises three critical sections: installing an operation's deadline, a cancellation callback applying now, and ending an operation. A stale callback can therefore only complete while its operation is current, or observe a bumped sequence and do nothing. Deadlock safety: the mutex is only held across conn.Set{Read,Write}Deadline calls, which return immediately even on a closed or blocked connection, so stop() only ever waits for a bounded fast setter, never for network I/O.
tests: all 10 pre-existing cancel/timeout tests in cancel_test.go pass in the full run
cancellation_callback_interleave.method: barrier setter with explicit entered/finished events; no sleep-based timing
cancellation_callback_interleave.fixture_notes: the fixture itself was corrected twice during development (a lock held while blocking caused a fixture deadlock; a gate that blocked the next operation's own installation caused a false pass); the final version is event-driven and drains application events between phases
